statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-78662 (GO-2026-6354): in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh, a malicious peer could flood requests on a channel that was not yet established and deadlock the whole connection. It is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.56.0: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6354, https://go.dev/issue/81316, https://go.dev/cl/826504. The advisory's vulnerable code is in the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh package: Dial, NewClientConn, NewControlClientConn, NewServerConn, (*channel).Accept, (*channel).handlePacket, (*channel).responseMessageReceived. Read every published alertmanager-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 36 builds, 0.31.1-r0 to the current 0.35.0-r2 (there is no 0.33.1-r4), each for x86_64 and aarch64 (72 packages), every download checked against the checksum in the package index. Each package holds two files, /usr/bin/alertmanager and /usr/bin/amtool, statically linked Go programs (no ELF interpreter and no dynamic section) with no ELF symbol table (linked with -ldflags "-s -w"; the Go function table is present), built with CGO_ENABLED=0. The Go build information lists golang.org/x/crypto v0.47.0 in 0.31.1-r0 to 0.31.1-r3, v0.49.0 in 0.31.1-r4, v0.50.0 in 0.31.1-r5 to 0.32.1-r1, v0.52.0 in 0.32.1-r2 to 0.32.2-r0, v0.53.0 in 0.33.0-r0 to 0.33.1-r1, v0.54.0 in 0.33.1-r2 to 0.33.1-r3, v0.55.0 in 0.33.1-r5 to 0.34.0-r3, v0.56.0 in 0.34.0-r4, v0.57.0 in 0.34.0-r5 to 0.34.1-r1 and v0.58.0 in 0.34.1-r2 to 0.35.0-r2. statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-78662 (GO-2026-6354): before golang.org/x/crypto v0.56.0, the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh connection handled channel requests and other channel messages on a channel that was opened but not yet confirmed or accepted, so a malicious SSH peer could flood such a channel with requests and deadlock the whole connection. v0.56.0 marks a channel established only once the peer confirms it or the local side accepts it, and until then drops every packet other than the open confirmation or failure. The Go vulnerability database lists Dial, NewClientConn, NewControlClientConn, NewServerConn and the channel's Accept, handlePacket and responseMessageReceived methods as the affected functions: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6354, https://go.dev/issue/81316, https://go.dev/cl/826504, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/1y3fb2np35U. The fix is commit a6cdac6, whose only change outside tests is to ssh/channel.go, and it is in v0.56.0 and not in v0.55.0: https://github.com/golang/crypto/commit/a6cdac60840750226b15617ac8858be44361b36b. We read every published build-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 91 versions, 2.6.4-r0 to the current 2.30.0-r0, for x86_64 and aarch64 (2.6.4-r0 is published for aarch64 only), after verifying each download against its index checksum. Version 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times for each architecture in the package index, every entry with the same source commit as 2.19.1-r0; the one copy the repository serves, which matches one of those entries' checksum, was read. Each package holds one program, the Go frontend program /usr/bin/build, besides the apk metadata. For every Go program in every build we read the Go build information and the function table (pclntab); each program's function table contains runtime.main. The frontend program links affected functions in every build: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh.Dial, NewClientConn and the channel's Accept and handlePacket methods, so the status follows the golang.org/x/crypto version. Every build before 2.20.0-r13 links golang.org/x/crypto v0.45.0 to v0.55.0 into it, inside the affected range; 2.20.0-r13 and every later build link v0.56.0 or newer, and the current 2.30.0-r0 links v0.59.0. As a check on the boundary, in the x86_64 build package the disassembly of (*channel).handlePacket in 2.20.0-r13 returns early for any message other than the open confirmation or failure, and (*channel).Accept contains the atomic store that marks the channel established, while in 2.20.0-r12 neither is present. The range ends at 2.20.0-r13, the first build with v0.56.0.

The build information lists golang.org/x/crypto v0.45.0 to v0.58.0, but no build's function table contains any function of the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh package. The only name under that path in any build is golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/terminal.init, the initializer of the separate ssh/terminal package, in 0.20.0-r0 to 0.21.0-r13. As a control, the same function-table search finds ssh.Dial, ssh.NewClientConn, ssh.(*channel).handlePacket and ssh.(*channel).Accept in the docker-buildx program of every published DHI docker-cli-buildx package for Alpine 3.23.

This package is the Go 1.26 toolchain. We read every published golang-1.26-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository, x86_64 and aarch64: 15 versions, 1.26.1-r2 to 1.26.11-r1, each matching its repository index checksum, together with the golang-1.26-dev-doc (15 versions, 1.26.1-r2 to 1.26.11-r1) and golang-1.26-dev-oci-config (15 versions, 1.26.1-r2 to 1.26.11-r1) packages built from the same source in that repository and the golang-1.26-dev-fips-oci-config (15 versions, 1.26.1-r2 to 1.26.11-r1) packages in the DHI Alpine security repository, on both architectures. It is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.56.0 by commit a6cdac6 (CL 826504, "ssh: drop traffic on undecided channels", which names CVE-2026-78662), whose only change outside tests is to ssh/channel.go: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6354, https://go.dev/cl/826504, https://github.com/golang/crypto/commit/a6cdac60840750226b15617ac8858be44361b36b, https://go.dev/issue/81316, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/1y3fb2np35U. The Go vulnerability database lists Dial, NewClientConn, NewControlClientConn, NewServerConn and the channel's Accept, handlePacket and responseMessageReceived methods in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh as the vulnerable functions. This package is the Go 1.26 toolchain. We read every published golang-1.26-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository, amd64 and arm64: 28 versions, 1.26.4-0 to 1.26.11-18, each matching its repository index checksum, together with the golang-1.26-dev-dbgsym (28 versions, 1.26.4-0 to 1.26.11-18) and golang-1.26-dev-oci-config (28 versions, 1.26.4-0 to 1.26.11-18) packages built from the same source in that repository and the golang-1.26-dev-fips-oci-config (28 versions, 1.26.4-0 to 1.26.11-18) packages in the DHI Debian security repository, on both architectures. The Go source tree each golang-1.26-dev package installs vendors these golang.org/x/crypto packages for the standard library under /usr/lib/go/src/vendor: chacha20, chacha20poly1305, cryptobyte, cryptobyte/asn1, internal/alias and internal/poly1305. golang.org/x/crypto/ssh is not among them, and /usr/lib/go/src/cmd/vendor holds no golang.org/x/crypto package. No package has a file or directory under a golang.org/x/crypto/ssh path. A Go function-table (pclntab) reader run on every Go program in the golang-1.26-dev packages (the go and gofmt commands and the tools under /usr/lib/go/pkg/tool) finds no function in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh, and finds runtime.main in each. The golang-1.26-dev-dbgsym packages hold separate debug files for those programs, with uncompressed debug sections; the byte search finds no golang.org/x/crypto/ssh string in them and finds runtime.main in each. The oci-config and fips-oci-config packages hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog. The same reader does find golang.org/x/crypto/ssh, including Dial, NewClientConn, NewServerConn and the channel's Accept and handlePacket methods, and the same byte search finds golang.org/x/crypto/ssh names including responseMessageReceived, which is inlined, in test programs we built for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 against golang.org/x/crypto v0.55.0 that call Dial, NewClientConn, NewServerConn and Accept. A Go program that uses golang.org/x/crypto/ssh takes it from its own golang.org/x/crypto requirement, not from the toolchain, so it is fixed by upgrading golang.org/x/crypto in that program.

A Go function-table (pclntab) reader run on every Go program in the golang-1.26 packages (the go and gofmt commands and the tools under /usr/lib/go/pkg/tool) finds no function in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh, and finds runtime.main in each. A byte search of every ELF file, which also catches inlined names and strings, finds no golang.org/x/crypto/ssh string of any kind. The golang-1.26-dbgsym packages hold separate debug files for those programs, with uncompressed debug sections; the byte search finds no golang.org/x/crypto/ssh string in them and finds runtime.main in each. The oci-config and fips-oci-config packages hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog. The same reader does find golang.org/x/crypto/ssh, including Dial, NewClientConn, NewServerConn and the channel's Accept and handlePacket methods, and the same byte search finds golang.org/x/crypto/ssh names including responseMessageReceived, which is inlined, in test programs we built for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 against golang.org/x/crypto v0.55.0 that call Dial, NewClientConn, NewServerConn and Accept. A Go program that uses golang.org/x/crypto/ssh takes it from its own golang.org/x/crypto requirement, not from the toolchain, so it is fixed by upgrading golang.org/x/crypto in that program.

CVE-2026-78662 (GO-2026-6354): before an SSH channel was established, a malicious peer could flood the channel's incoming requests and deadlock the entire connection; the fix drops every packet other than the open confirmation or failure until the channel is usable. The flaw is in the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh package and is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.56.0. Sources: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6354, https://go.dev/issue/81316, https://go.dev/cl/826504, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/1y3fb2np35U. This package is the Go 1.27 toolchain. The Go source tree it ships vendors a few golang.org/x/crypto packages for the standard library under /usr/lib/go/src/vendor, and its cmd tree vendors no golang.org/x/crypto package. In no published build is golang.org/x/crypto/ssh among them. We checked every published golang-1.27-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository (1.27.0-0 to 1.27.4-18, amd64 and arm64), together with the golang-1.27-dev-oci-config, golang-1.27-dev-fips-oci-config (from the DHI security repository) and golang-1.27-dev-dbgsym (debug symbol) packages built from the same source, 200 packages in all, each matching the repository index checksum: none contains a golang.org/x/crypto/ssh directory or source file, and no ELF file in them (including the go and gofmt commands and the tools under /usr/lib/go/pkg/tool) contains the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh import path. The debug files in the golang-1.27-dev-dbgsym packages carry no function table of their own (their .gopclntab section is empty), so for them we read their symbol tables instead, which list runtime.main and no golang.org/x/crypto/ssh symbol. That byte search is backed by a function-table check: we read the Go function table (pclntab) of the 10 Go executables in every build (the go and gofmt commands and the eight tools under /usr/lib/go/pkg/tool), and none lists a golang.org/x/crypto/ssh function, including the advisory's Dial, NewClientConn, NewControlClientConn, NewServerConn, channel.Accept, channel.handlePacket and channel.responseMessageReceived; the same listing finds runtime.main in every executable and vendored golang.org/x/crypto functions, such as vendor/golang.org/x/crypto/cryptobyte, in every go command, so it does see vendored golang.org/x/crypto code. As a check against a vulnerable release, the same function-table reader and byte search find golang.org/x/crypto/ssh code, including Dial, NewClientConn, NewServerConn and channel.handlePacket, in a test program we built for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 against golang.org/x/crypto v0.51.0 that calls ssh.Dial, ssh.NewClientConn and ssh.NewServerConn. The byte search also finds no golang.org/x/crypto/ssh path in the debug files. A Go program that uses golang.org/x/crypto/ssh takes it from its own golang.org/x/crypto requirement, not from the toolchain, so it is fixed by upgrading golang.org/x/crypto in that program.
